hypothesis: Pigment-network states are repeatedly reachable through regulatory/flux changes
chun_result_basis: 8/8 independent mechanistic clusters show regulatory/flux evidence; 6/6 red-direction clusters show higher anthocyanin; no positive structural-loss requirement in informative clusters
claim_boundary: supports recurrent accessibility, not a natural mechanism frequency

hypothesis: Anthocyanin-like red/pink floral state generally enables colder climatic niche expansion in Camellia
chun_result_basis: original exact-taxonomy 50-species A vs W tests were null; after minimal provenance cleaning of four Tuberculatae record instances representing two implausible shared coordinates, A-W remains null: BIO1 P=0.805; BIO6 median P=0.526; BIO6 q05 P=0.252; BIO1 IQR P=0.705. Specimen-only and synthetic-topology sensitivities had also not supported a general cold-tail shift.
remaining_test: apply the same record-level provenance gate to all tail metrics and then restrict future work to branch-level conditional tests
claim_boundary: do not retain as a genus-wide primary hypothesis; cleaning changes tail effect size but does not produce significance

hypothesis: Anthocyanin deployment facilitates cold/UV adaptation only in particular lineages or ecological contexts
chun_result_basis: macro literature contains support, null and counterexample units; genus-wide A-W thermal means are null; the apparent Tuberculatae cold-edge event was an occurrence-provenance artefact rather than evidence for a colour-independent boundary shift
remaining_test: validated primary nuclear-tree branch-event tests using provenance-admitted environmental boundaries and mechanistic pigment rather than visible hue
claim_boundary: plausible only conditionally; every candidate boundary event must first pass occurrence provenance

hypothesis: Yellow state is unusually historically/geographically constrained
chun_result_basis: Fan Data S1 species analysis: Y 22/22 confined to South China/Southwest China/Vietnam versus non-Y 64/84; one-sided Fisher P=0.00552; A vs W geography P=1.0; GBIF thermal Y sample remains only two South-China Chrysantha species
remaining_test: nuclear-tree ancestral range/transition reconstruction and broader occurrence audit
claim_boundary: supports geographic constraint, not a yellow thermal optimum

hypothesis: Red/pink anthocyanin-like state expands beyond southern ancestral belt more readily than white
chun_result_basis: Fan Data S1 species geography: A 21/28 south-only vs W 43/56; OR=0.907, Fisher P=1.0
claim_boundary: A and W are indistinguishable in this source-geography contrast

hypothesis: Visible flower-colour states are strongly structured by lineage/history rather than being distributed independently across Camellia
chun_result_basis: Fan Data S1 deterministic species table excluding non-section Vietnam rows: 98 species across 17 traditional sections; section×colour Pearson chi2=178.646, Cramer's V=0.955, 100000-shuffle permutation P<1e-5; e.g. sect. Camellia 22/23 A, sect. Chrysantha 13/13 Y, sect. Thea 14/14 W
remaining_test: replace traditional-section proxy with admitted nuclear-tree phylogenetic signal / transition model
claim_boundary: traditional sections are not assumed monophyletic; the former section×cold-tail association is explicitly excluded because it was driven by invalid extreme occurrences

hypothesis: Molecular accessibility generates variants while ecology/history filters which states persist macroevolutionarily
chun_result_basis: strong micro recurrence contrasts with weak genus-wide red/cold evidence; yellow geography and section-colour structure are strong, while the occurrence audit shows that environmental-boundary candidates require an independent provenance layer before filtering can be inferred
remaining_test: provenance-admitted environment/pollinator boundaries -> latent state -> primary-tree transition/event model
claim_boundary: supported as synthesis pattern; causal filtering factors not yet separated

hypothesis: The exact pigment-network nodes labile within development/cultivars are preferentially reused on macroevolutionary colour-transition branches
chun_result_basis: cross-scale accessibility pattern motivates this but macro branch gene assignments are not yet available
remaining_test: primary nuclear tree + transition mapping + raw RNAseq/common ortholog node enrichment

hypothesis: Pollinator sensory environment helps determine which accessible pigment/spectral states persist
chun_result_basis: species-level pollination evidence is heterogeneous; same visible red can be bird-associated or insect-associated
remaining_test: phylogenetic meta-regression on spectrum/UV, nectar, season and effective pollination
claim_boundary: do not infer from human colour categories alone

hypothesis: Anthocyanin-like A lineages occupy narrower thermal breadth than W lineages
chun_result_basis: OpenTree synthetic topology + Grafen BM-PGLS previously gave BIO1 IQR A-W=-1.17 C P=0.000233 while raw species-label tests were non-significant; provenance cleaning altered Tuberculatae breadth values and this synthetic-tree signal has not yet been rerun on the cleaned matrix
remaining_test: rerun only after full occurrence provenance cleaning and preferably on a primary dated nuclear tree
claim_boundary: do not promote from topology-only/pre-provenance sensitivity

hypothesis: Human-visible W/A/Y states merge distinct biochemical, sensory and ecological states and therefore lose macroevolutionarily relevant information
chun_result_basis: most directly, red C. japonica and red C. rusticana have different pollination strategies/sensory signals; mechanistic ledger shows multiple regulatory/flux routes to superficially similar less-red/white states and yellow C. nitidissima combines flavonol and carotenoid deployment. Thermal niche contrasts are secondary until they pass the new provenance gate.
remaining_test: build species latent pigment/spectral state matrix and compare predictive/phylogenetic fit against W/A/Y on primary nuclear trees
claim_boundary: supports visible hue as a lossy deterministic proxy, not yet superiority of a particular latent-state model

hypothesis: White is often an accessible retained-pathway reservoir/bridge rather than a terminal pigment-loss state
chun_result_basis: published visible root is white; exact climate subset W spans 9/10 observed sections versus A 2/10 and Y 1/10; all informative mechanistic clusters implicate regulatory/flux changes and none require wholesale structural loss
remaining_test: nuclear-tree stochastic maps with root/state-frequency/sampling controls plus pathway-retention evidence on W->coloured branches
claim_boundary: broad white distribution can arise by ancestral retention alone; do not call white an evolutionary hub until transition centrality exceeds null expectation

hypothesis: Ecological function can change while coarse visible hue remains similar
chun_result_basis: red C. japonica is bird-associated whereas red C. rusticana is insect/bee-associated with distinct UV/fluorescence cues; this direct sensory/pollination contrast does not depend on the GBIF thermal data. Their thermal contrast remains preliminary until record-level provenance audit.
remaining_test: expand spectra/UV/pollinator matrix across independent same-hue species pairs and apply the occurrence provenance gate before adding niche contrasts
claim_boundary: one within-genus case establishes non-uniqueness of hue-to-function mapping, not its genus-wide frequency

hypothesis: Extreme climatic range limits are generated by rare lineage-specific boundary shifts rather than broad visible-colour regimes
chun_result_basis: artifact-level point audit shows both C. rhytidocarpa and C. tuberculata share the same two extreme coordinates 42.9N 125.14E (BIO6 -20.65 C) and 38.073254N 104.69114E (BIO6 -12.95 C), grossly outside independent native-range evidence. Removing only these four record instances changes q05 from -14.105 to +1.425 C and -16.415 to +0.400 C and eliminates the section signal (AW section R2=0.235 P=0.189; null AIC best).
remaining_test: search for other candidate branch-edge events only after provenance/range validation
claim_boundary: reject Tuberculatae as evidence for a biological extreme cold-edge shift; this does not reject true rare edge events elsewhere

hypothesis: A few occurrence-provenance errors can dominate lower-tail climatic niche metrics in sparsely sampled narrow-ranged Camellia
chun_result_basis: two implausible records per Tuberculatae taxon moved BIO6 q05 by +15.53 C in C. rhytidocarpa and +16.815 C in C. tuberculata when removed; both taxa shared the exact two extreme coordinates and the country-only GBIF filter admitted all records
remaining_test: run automated K-coldest metadata/coordinate-reuse/leverage audit across all admitted taxa and quantify how often tail metrics change materially
claim_boundary: demonstrated for the Tuberculatae case; prevalence across Camellia is not yet known

hypothesis: Occurrence-derived climatic boundary events require a stricter evidence gate than niche centroids before macroevolutionary lead/lag inference
chun_result_basis: the Tuberculatae false-positive passed accepted-name, country and GBIF geospatial filters yet failed independent native-range plausibility and point-leverage audit
remaining_test: apply accepted-name + provenance metadata + range plausibility + coordinate-reuse + leave-one-record/locality-out checks before admitting any branch boundary event
claim_boundary: an analysis can be statistically correct but biologically invalid if the environmental event itself is artefactual
